releaseSet.reason: macOS Build 62 is the current notarized Sparkle prerelease. Windows 0.0.27 remains the published stable installer, while the DNS port-owner fix is source-ready as 0.0.29 on release/windows and has not been represented as a published binary.

provenance.audit: The signed artifact is retained and verified. The immutable legacy tag was created at the Windows 0.0.27 commit because the old macOS release command omitted an explicit target.

update.reason: 0.0.27 is the current published installer; the signed automatic update channel has not yet been promoted beyond 0.0.25.

knownLimitations: Automatic update users remain on 0.0.25 until the audited windows-updates channel is explicitly promoted.
The 0.0.28 release exists only as a draft and is not a customer release.
The 0.0.29 DNS port-owner fix is source-ready but remains unpublished until a signed Windows build and real-machine gate pass.

fixes: Reconciles a stale Tono-owned core through the authenticated Service before checking DNS TCP/UDP port 53.
Never terminates third-party DNS or proxy processes; an external owner still produces an actionable failure.
Reports TCP and UDP ownership consistently instead of showing contradictory diagnostics.
releaseGate: Build and sign the Windows installer from release/windows.
Verify the 127.0.0.1:53 stale-owner recovery and third-party-owner refusal on Windows 11.
Publish v0.0.29 only after artifact and updater-channel checks pass.

summary: Notarized arm64 app and Sparkle Ed25519 enclosure signature verified.
Keeps WeChat TCP/80 on Tono-Exit while reviewed TCP/443, UDP/443 and TCP/8080 traffic can use the China direct application route.
The immutable legacy tag points at a Windows commit; the artifact remains available and the mismatch is preserved here as an audit record.
Current published Windows installer.
Improves coexistence with VMware, VirtualBox, Hyper-V, WSL, Docker and other virtual adapters.
The automatic Windows update channel remains independently pinned to 0.0.25.
Fixes the connect-timeout handler aborting its own task, which stranded the UI in Connecting and killed the auto-reconnect chain.
A failed kill-switch release now keeps the armed state visible instead of showing notConnected over a live WFP barrier (and no longer lets Quit skip the release).
Resets network-monitor seeds on every connect success, ending the deterministic connect/teardown flapping loop after network events.
Flushes the Windows resolver cache after DNS enable so cached real-IP answers can no longer defeat the fake-ip probe (up to 7s wasted or a spurious connect failure).
WFP boot restore installs the current filter set before sweeping legacy sublayers, closing the v1-upgrade fail-open window; unreadable intent now arms the emergency block.
Connect path parallelized: five prep probes run concurrently, bootstrap host resolution is parallel (worst case ~32s to ~2s), controller readiness polls on an adaptive grid.
First build whose NSIS payload passed the full extraction gate: exactly one stable Mihomo, no alpha, no Unix helpers.
Moves every privileged Service IPC request onto a dedicated two-worker Tokio runtime so synchronous Windows pipe and Service Control Manager work cannot starve the Tauri runtime.
Keeps an IPC request alive after the calling future is dropped, preserving late-arm reconciliation and Kill Switch safety semantics.
Sets a four-worker floor for the Tauri runtime and reports live elapsed time while Starting Kill Switch is still in progress.
Retains the Test 4 TUN interface-alias fix, startup cleanup, initial-failure release and verified-session fail-closed behavior.
The extracted NSIS payload contains the new Service hashes and IPC-runtime evidence; application, installer and uninstaller icons exactly match the Tono source icon.
Unsigned cross-build for limited Windows real-machine acceptance only; broad customer rollout remains blocked pending the full Windows checklist.
Do not continue customer testing: a Windows real-machine test shows the native App window becoming unresponsive immediately after entering Starting Kill Switch.
Superseded by Test 5; retained only as an immutable audit record.
Resolves the Mihomo TUN alias with ConvertInterfaceAliasToLuid so the Windows traffic-locking stage no longer fails with Windows error 123.
Retains startup cleanup for unverified stale Kill Switch state, safe initial-failure release and fail-closed handling for verified sessions.
Centers the dashboard content, replaces the old eye/bird-like center glyph with the official Tono ribbon mark and reduces the glow effect.
Extracted NSIS payload Service and Mihomo hashes match the build inputs; application, installer and uninstaller icons match the Tono source icon.
Unsigned cross-build for limited Windows real-machine testing only; full Windows validation remains pending.
Do not use for connection testing: the Service resolves the Mihomo TUN alias with the wrong Windows API, so locking traffic fails with Windows error 123.
Superseded by Test 4; retained only as an immutable audit record.
Does not restore an unverified stale Kill Switch intent merely because the Tono GUI opens.
Safely restores DNS and releases WFP protection when the first connection attempt fails, while verified tunnel failures remain fail-closed.
Adds owner/session-gated Kill Switch verification and advances the Service protocol to revision 8.
Replaces application, tray, installer, uninstaller and web icons with Tono branding; extracted NSIS payload hashes and icons were verified.

A Test 2 record captured during its brief Locked-before-verification window remains fail-closed on first migration because the legacy format cannot distinguish it from an established session; Restore normal network or Disconnect clears it.
Do not use: this build may restore stale unverified Kill Switch state when the GUI opens and interrupt all network access.
Superseded by Test 3; retained only as an immutable audit record.
Accepts canonical Windows extended-length core paths under Program Files without weakening the Service allowlist.
Requires per-machine installs under Program Files and gives legacy custom-location users an explicit uninstall-and-reinstall path.
Accepts traffic-policy v1 and v2 with exact reviewed web host TCP/443 rules.
Claude process rules precede all DIRECT rules; Anthropic, Claude and Tono domains remain protected.
Uses the same bounded adaptive gVisor TCP buffer policy as Mac Build 37.
Cross-build and automated tests passed; Windows real-machine verification remains required.
Seven-day exact-host China direct canary with independent cloud rollback.
Claude App, Claude Code and Anthropic official traffic retain proxy precedence.
Native WeChat and 16 reviewed video hostnames use exact host, pinned IPv4 and bounded port rules.
Experimental Mihomo v1.19.29-tono-gvisor-adaptive.1 uses bounded adaptive gVisor TCP buffers.
First hardened Windows x64 NSIS test build.
Cross-compiled and packaged on macOS; Windows verification remains required.
Unsigned test artifact; automatic updater is disabled.
Supports traffic-policy v1 only and is not paired with the current v2 canary.
Established the Sparkle 2 signed automatic-update baseline.
Added six-hour checks and manual Check for Updates.
Retained mainland weak-network timeout and bounded retry behavior.
Stored 39 retained macOS package and checksum assets in a private GitHub Release draft.
Build 33 fixed ambiguous node-switch config reload timeouts while remaining fail-closed.
Private rollback and audit inventory; not a customer download channel.
Private notarized binary backup used to diagnose mainland connection failures.
Introduced local traffic audit for helper, Kill Switch, TUN, DNS and Reality stage diagnosis.
